questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very interested in going to McGill to experience the English and French bilingual study environment. I had also heard very good things about McGill as university, with interesting legal courses etc. I also really wanted to go to Canada for the longest time, so that also played a big part in my motivation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say, it was relatively easy. McGill arranged seminars for newcomers, where we received all the important information in terms of our enrollment and life at McGill in general.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assisted a lot in the beginning. They arranged events and clearly communicated by mail. One thing is, you do not get a lot of information about your specific courses beforehand. You really just have to show up on the first with little to no preparation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. I found my housing on AirBnb, which was a bit more expensive, but also very convnient, since the host was available and flexible in terms of renting dates. Other than that, there was also a lot of facebook groups, with plenty of options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I can really reccommend living off campus, since you also get to live in and experience other parts of Montreal. Public transport in Montreal is great, so don't be afraid of not living right next to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was relatively simple. I just had to get the student card. As a Danish citizen, you are exempt from the mandatory McGill health inssurance, since you qualify for RAMQ (Quebec's public health insurance), which is great since you do not have to pay. However, the process of applying for exemption can be a bit complicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a student service building at campus, and they were always ready to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: My registration worked fine. The only problem is that KU had to pre-approve all the courses, so if I switched courses, I would have to get them pre-approved again.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be patient and be prepared for their website, online services etc. to be a bit more old school and complicated than KU.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was enrolled as a bachelor student at McGill, eventhough I'm a master student at UCPH. This is because you for the most part need a BA degree to even enroll at Law studies in Canada.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: IT was much more focused on class discussion and more abstract ideas. It was definitely less "technical" and "applied level" than UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environment & the law
Indigenous People & the State
Droit Public International
Comparative Federalism
International Development Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can really recommend Comparative Federalism since you get a better understanding of the Canadian legal system, but also can contribute with your own experiences in federal countries.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Restaurant, bar and supermarket prices are generally cheaper than Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tons of differents sports were available, even if you did not sign up for a specific team. I played pick-up badminton weekly at the university gym. When the weather got better, I played a lot of football outdoors on the university pitches.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can really reccommend doing a sport or joining a student association, since there are plenty options.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I personally took the opportunity to visit differents parts of Canada, such as Toronto or Quebec City. I also went skiing a couple of times.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture in Montreal is incredible. People are so polite and hospitable. It is so easy to adjust to the local culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My best tip is to just join student clubs or do sports. Also do the international student introductory events. A great opportunity to meet new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality, friendliness and openess.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Do not be afraid of trying out new things, wether it's sports, food or travel
2. Start conversations with strangers. Locals are very open-minded, and this is not considered awkward or weird as it is in Denmark
3. Participate in class since it can help improve your English or French

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be a bit patient with figuring out the McGill administrative system. It can be a bit confusing if you want to get you paperowrk done, but there is always help to get.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The overall experience was just incredible. I got to meet a lot of new people and travel.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The weather. During winter time, Montreal gets incredibly cold. Be prepared for many weeks with -15 degrees or lower.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
